summary: Describes how to run WebSockets over a single stream of an HTTP/3 connection. The mechanism already existed for HTTP/2, and only the HTTP-version-specific details needed to be specified. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: WebSockets can now ride on the newest web connection type, like putting an old phone line on a new road.

questions: how do websockets work over http/3
subtitle: How the WebSocket-over-HTTP/2 mechanism carries over to HTTP/3 with one registered setting.

tldr.problem: RFC 8441 defines how to run WebSockets over a single stream of an HTTP/2 connection. The same mechanism is useful for HTTP/3, but the version-specific details were not specified.
tldr.mechanism: HTTP/3 reuses Extended CONNECT with identical semantics and registers the SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL setting for HTTP/3 with value 0x08.
tldr.outcome: WebSockets can be bootstrapped over HTTP/3 the same way as over HTTP/2, with stream closure standing in for TCP connection closure.

today: RFC 9220 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata shows no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Porting an HTTP/2 Extension
sections.content:
RFC 8441, "Bootstrapping WebSockets with HTTP/2", defines an extension that is also useful in HTTP/3. The extension uses an HTTP/2 setting, and Appendix A.3 of the HTTP/3 specification gives guidance on what changes, if any, are appropriate when porting settings from HTTP/2 to HTTP/3.

This RFC is short because almost everything carries over unchanged.
sections.plainLanguage: A trick that already worked on the older road works on the new road too. This note just fills in the small details.

sections.title: Extended CONNECT and the Setting
sections.content:
RFC 8441 defines, for running the WebSocket Protocol (RFC 6455) over one stream of an HTTP/2 connection, an Extended CONNECT method. It adds a :protocol pseudo-header field and new semantics for :path and :authority, plus a setting a server sends to let the client use Extended CONNECT.

The semantics of the pseudo-header fields and the setting are identical to HTTP/2. Because HTTP/3 settings must be registered separately, this document registers SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL with the value 0x08 (decimal 8), the same as in HTTP/2.
sections.plainLanguage: The server shows a sign that says Special requests welcome. The sign looks the same as before, but it needs to be registered in the new building's list.

sections.title: Unknown Protocols and Stream Closure
sections.content:
If a server advertises Extended CONNECT but receives a request whose :protocol value is unknown or unsupported, it SHOULD respond with a 501 (Not Implemented) status code. It MAY add detail with a "problem details" response (RFC 7807).

HTTP/3 stream closure is analogous to TCP connection closure in RFC 6455. An orderly TCP-level closure is represented as a FIN bit on the stream, and RST exceptions are represented with a stream error of type H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED.
sections.plainLanguage: If someone asks for something the server does not know, it politely says it cannot do that. Hanging up nicely and hanging up in a hurry each have their own signal.

sections.title: Security and IANA Registration
sections.content:
The document introduces no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 8441.

IANA registers a new entry in the "HTTP/3 Settings" registry: value 0x08, name SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL, default 0, status permanent, specification this document, change controller IETF.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing new to worry about. The setting just gets its official entry in the list.
